# Git History Privacy Scan Draft

Historical object scan executed successfully. Independent checker PASS receipt supplied by the user: exact replay of all 435 groups / 21,201 records, 93 commits, 589 unique blobs and 74 Chin-home path occurrences. This receipt verifies the saved snapshot evidence, not later commits or credential validity. User authorized committing only this report and the section-6 board; scanner source/evidence unchanged and not rerun.

Recommendations: real private home-path literals occur in history; review a separately approved clean export or history rewrite before public distribution. No rewrite is performed here. Credential candidates remain unknown, not live-confirmed; rotate only after determining a candidate is a real credential. This report is not a clean-history certificate.

## Recount And Context Receipt

Replayed all immutable saved commit IDs using only Git historical objects. Exact commit closures, 12,991 tree entries, 589 unique blobs and all category totals reproduced. Ledger integrity verified: 435 groups contain exactly 21,201 expanded full commit-ID match entries. No raw private path or email detected in the report. Local refs unchanged since snapshot. This same-agent verification is not the independent main checker.

Concrete path findings: 74 historical occurrences contain the Chin home prefix; 8 other concrete Mac-path occurrences have unverified ownership; 17 additional occurrences have detector context. Concrete path spelling is confirmed, not evidence of actual filesystem access. All private parts remain redacted in the complete ledger below.

Potential credential assignments: 1,121 historical occurrences, of which 616 have nearby fixture/demo/attack context and 505 remain unknown. Nearby context does not establish a published demo credential or validity, so all remain potential candidates. Another 806 assignments and 93 token-pattern matches are synthetic/demo-looking, publication unverified. Potential-real emails: 58 occurrences; example/synthetic emails: 19,024, including 180 Chin-related metadata occurrences. Credential activation or ownership is not tested.

No Git command failure, unreadable blob, binary blob or gitlink encountered. Coverage limitations remain: quoted credential assignments and recognized token signatures are heuristic, not exhaustive secret detection; unquoted/obfuscated credentials, encoded archives, non-email author names and expired reflog entries are not comprehensively assessed. No confirmed live credential finding or clean-history certification is claimed.

## Scope And Method

Local refs include remote-tracking refs, tags, stash and other refs plus HEAD. Reflog tips were snapshotted separately before traversal; reflog-only means ancestor closure minus local-ref closure. No fetch, network, checkout, rewrite or credential/environment file inspection. Git objects only; unrelated worktree changes preserved. Unique blobs decoded once, all historical tree occurrences mapped. Messages, filenames, author/committer header emails and signature headers scanned.

Approved ephemeral directory: `[REDACTED private-temp]`. Snapshot basename: `aegis_history_scan_snapshot.json`. Scanner basename: `aegis_history_privacy_scan.py`.

## Limits And Classification

Heuristic candidates, not proof of valid credentials. Unknown credential-looking values remain potential-real; synthetic/demo-looking values do not prove credentials were publicly published. Detector-literal labels require context review and are not automatic safe exclusions. Chin-related is an email lexical flag, not verified ownership. All private values withheld; stable SHA-256 prefixes correlate equal values without exposing them. Binary blobs receive the same raw printable ASCII regex coverage through UTF-8 replacement decoding; byte offsets are not reported, LF-based line numbers apply. No archive decompression, OCR, encrypted-content interpretation or semantic obfuscation decoding. Nonblob gitlinks flag external contents unavailable without network. No unreachable objects beyond reflog closure scanned. Reflog snapshot uses Git-visible entries; expired entries cannot be recovered.
